title: bonsai.bug/1
description: A bug (contract §7.3; plan P-T-6023): one known defect someone has seen or proven, where it stands, and who found, filed and fixed it. One markdown file per bug, named <id>.md or <id>-<slug>.md, in the folder bonsai.yaml names under documents.bug (absent: bugs/ beside documents.bugs's file; both absent, work/bugs/). This schema describes its YAML frontmatter as a reader returns it (JSON); the body is free text: how to repeat it, what was seen, notes. Written by agents (bonsai bug, from Bonsai 1.1.0, writes every move and its fields); read by Bonsai (bonsai check holds each file to this schema and no two files to one id; check --write builds the bugs page, bonsai.bugs/1, from them), the studio and agents. A writer writes every field below, in this order, null or {} where it does not apply (contract §2.2); a reader treats a missing field as null and keeps an unknown one. The frontmatter follows the format-1 YAML rules (contract §2.4).

format.description: The version line, always the first key. A reader that meets a newer major (bonsai.bug/2) says "format too new" and reads nothing else (contract §2.2). In a file made from a template the line carries a one-line pointer back as a trailing comment (contract §2.8), which is a comment and not part of the value.

id.description: The bug's id: BUG- and 3 to 6 digits, unique in the workspace and never reused, in every project (one prefix; an old id from a register with another prefix is kept in was). The file is named after it, <id>.md or <id>-<slug>.md; written plain, never quoted.

title.description: What goes wrong, as a person sees it, on one line.
examples: The sessions cache's version number is not tied to the build

status.description: Where the bug stands. A closed list: open (seen or proven, not fixed), fixed (a commit fixed it: fixed_in), wontfix (known, not a bug, or not to be fixed: why), watched (seen once and not repeated, a flaky test among them: why). A new bug starts at open. Agents make every move: open to fixed, wontfix or watched; watched to open or fixed; fixed and wontfix back to open (it came back). Its line carries no comment in format 1.

area.description: The part of the project it is in, a few words, as the project names its parts; null for none.

where.description: Where it goes wrong: a file and line, a command, a screen; with how sure the finder was where it helps (pointed: the line was read; said: only a report says so). null when not known.

found_by.description: Who or what found it: a role and task, a message id, a person, a CI run. null when not known (a bug carried over from an old register that named no one).

filed_by.description: Who wrote this file: an agent's address (role@task, or a role), or person. null for a bug carried over from an old register that did not say.

fixed_by.description: Who marked it fixed, in the same form as filed_by; null while it is not fixed, and for a carried-over bug that did not say.

fixed_in.description: The commit or commits that fixed it, with a few words on how where it helps; null while it is not fixed.
examples: fee1e13a (a record whose newest is older is read again)

task.description: The task that fixed it, or the task it is being fixed under; null for none.

was.description: Its id in the register it was carried over from, when that id was another (TB-012 became BUG-012); null for a bug filed here.

why.description: Why it is wontfix or watched, one sentence; null for an open or fixed bug, unless a reason helps.
examples: A deliberate fail-closed over-refusal, documented in the guard's tests

created.description: The day the bug was filed, YYYY-MM-DD as text (a date stays text to every contract reader, contract §2.4), the UTC day (contract §23), taken from bonsai now --day. A bug carried over from an old register keeps the day its row named, else the day of the move (with was set).

closed.description: The day it was fixed or set wontfix (the kind's stamp: fixed and wontfix set it), YYYY-MM-DD as text (a date stays text to every contract reader, contract §2.4), the UTC day (contract §23), taken from bonsai now --day; null while it is open or watched. A fixed or wontfix bug with no closed day is allowed only with was set (a carried-over bug whose old row named no day): bonsai check holds that.

labels.description: Everything else, as a map of label name to value (contract §5): each name is <namespace>.<name> with one dot; each value is of its definition's kind, or null when empty. {} when the bug carries none.
